crawl._recent_lookback_note: Days back to scan for recent award ACTIONS (mods/obligations/options). 120 lets the cockpit bucket by action age: 0-30, 30-90, and 90+ days. Raise to widen the 90+ bucket.
crawl._expiring_window_note: 90 = at least 3 months of lead time (never forecast tighter). 730 = out to 24 months. Cockpit buckets: near-term 3-6mo (90-180d), mid-term 6-12mo (180-365d), long-term 12mo+ (365d+).
crawl._usa_reliability_note: usa_timeout_secs caps each USASpending request; crawl_deadline_secs is a hard wall-clock cap on the whole USASpending crawl so a degraded upstream cannot run the crawl for an hour. Partial results are still enriched and committed.
crawl._summary_wait_note: Hard cap on waiting for the Anthropic summaries batch. On timeout the step keeps existing summaries and lets the crawl/enrich results commit; new summaries backfill next run. Prevents an intermittent batch hang from blocking commits.
crawl._enrich_note: HigherGov enrichment (bd_enrich.py) looks up each aligned award/expiring lead by government Award ID and backfills contracting-office contacts, incumbent identity (UEI/CAGE), and vehicle. Incremental (skips already-enriched ids). Base usage is 10,000 records/month; the per-run cap and incremental skip keep spend bounded. Needs HIGHERGOV_API_KEY.
crawl._sam_poc_note: Company enrichment runs for EVERY aligned lead using the awardee UEI USASpending returns directly (Recipient UEI), so company info lands on all cards, not just HigherGov-matched ones. Per UEI: (1) HigherGov /awardee/ -> company profile (website, location, employees, founded, business/socioeconomic types, HigherGov company page); (2) SAM.gov Entity API -> company POC names (public tier: names/titles only). The website/domain drives precise ZoomInfo/LinkedIn lookups. Government contracting-office POCs are intentionally NOT collected; focus is the company and its contacts. Needs HIGHERGOV_API_KEY and SAM_API_KEY (Entity read-public). Incumbent identity is set for all leads immediately; profiles fill as max_sam_poc_per_run allows.
crawl._min_award_note: Lowered from $1M to $250K in v1.4. Most Ignitec prime references are under $2M, and task-order-sized work is where SDB status is most competitive. The cockpit still buckets by value; a low floor widens the funnel without forcing pursuit.
crawl._set_aside_note: cannot_prime_set_asides are set-asides Ignitec is not eligible to hold (8(a) pending not active; no SDVOSB/WOSB/HUBZone). On the EXPIRING/recompete play these are sub-only targets, flagged in scoring, NOT filtered out. On the RECENT-AWARD play set-aside is irrelevant since subbing under any prime is allowed.

gate_bands.feasibility_check: Run before scoring, not scored. Binary. Any failure is an immediate no-bid: submission mechanics, pricing gate (Anand sign-off), mandatory artifacts, named personnel, legal restrictions. Current workload/capacity is NOT scored; it is filtered at sourcing.
gate_bands.note: 2.6+ pursue (prime/preferred sub); 2.2-2.5 pursue as sub; 2.0-2.1 conditional/RFI only; below 2.0 no-bid. Any single gate at 0 is an immediate no-bid. Feasibility failure is an immediate no-bid and is not scored. RFI/Sources Sought touching a Tier 1 or Tier 2 lane responds regardless of score.

experience._note: Data-grounded past performance for priority scoring, reconciled to MNL v2.9 (2026-07). proven_agencies/naics/psc raise experience-affinity; prime_relationships are primes Ignitec has actually subcontracted to (strongest signal for the subcontracting play). Substring, case-insensitive.

scoring._note: Priority score 0-100 -> tiers. Data lists live in 'experience'; these are the tier cutoffs. Tier A = review first, B = worth a look, C = long tail (hidden by default in the cockpit). Tune the cutoffs to widen or tighten the review queue.
